record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can Savitch’s theorem be improved by proving that every nondeterministic space-s computation can be simulated in deterministic space o(s^2), rather than only the known O(s^2) bound?

evidence.quote: Savitch’s Theorem [Sav70], which states that NSPACE(s) ⊆ SPACE(O(s2)), is one of the bedrocks of space complexity, but it is not known to be tight.
Problem 4. Try to improve Savitch’s Theorem: prove NSPACE(s) ⊆ SPACE(o(s2)).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a function s: ℕ → ℕ with s(n) ≥ log n, let SPACE(s(n)) denote the class of languages decided by a deterministic Turing machine using O(s(n)) work-tape cells, and let NSPACE(s(n)) denote the class of languages decided by a nondeterministic Turing machine using O(s(n)) work-tape cells. Savitch's theorem asserts the inclusion NSPACE(s(n)) ⊆ SPACE(s(n)²).

Prove or disprove the following strengthening of Savitch's theorem: every language in NSPACE(s(n)) can be decided by a deterministic Turing machine using o(s(n)²) space; that is,
    NSPACE(s(n)) ⊆ SPACE(o(s(n)²)).
Equivalently, exhibit a deterministic simulation of nondeterministic s-space computations whose space usage is asymptotically strictly smaller than s² (for instance, s² / ω(1), or s^{2−ε} for some ε > 0), or rule out the existence of such a simulation.
artifact.status_search_result: Savitch's theorem (1970) gives NSPACE(s) ⊆ SPACE(s²), and no asymptotic improvement to o(s²) is known. Standard references and lecture notes describe the quadratic bound as the best known, and improving it is widely cited as a long-standing open problem in space complexity.

status_evidence.title: Savitch's theorem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Savitch's theorem (1970) states NSPACE(f(n)) ⊆ DSPACE(f(n)^2); no improvement to this quadratic bound is known.
status_evidence.claim: The quadratic bound of Savitch's theorem has not been improved.

status_evidence.title: Complexity Dojo/Savitch's Theorem - Complexity Zoo
status_evidence.snippet: Savitch's Theorem from 1970 has not been improved; whether the squaring is necessary remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Whether NSPACE(s) ⊆ SPACE(o(s^2)) holds is an open question.
